# Create manifest so QIIME knows where the reads are

```{bash}
mkdir -p ../output/eDNA_mapping
cd ../output/eDNA_mapping

raw=$(realpath ../../data/raw)

# manifest: sample name, R1 path, R2 path
printf "sample-id\tforward-absolute-filepath\treverse-absolute-filepath\n" > manifest.tsv


for sample in Site1J_S99 Site1L_S101 Site1U_S114 Site1a_S83 Site1aa_S130 Site1b_S84 Site1bb_S139 Site1c_S85 Site1cc_S140 Site1d_S86 Site1dd_S141 Site1e_S91 Site1ee_S142 Site1f_S92 Site1g_S93 Site1h_S94 Site1k_S100 Site1m_S102 Site1n_S103 Site1o_S104 Site1p_S105 Site1q_S106 Site1r_S111 Site1s_S112 Site1t_S113 Site1v_S117 Site1w_S118 Site1x_S119 Site1y_S120 Site1z_S129 Site5J_S107 Site5L_S109 Site5a_S87 Site5aa_S132 Site5b_S88 Site5bb_S133 Site5c_S89 Site5cc_S134 Site5d_S90 Site5dd_S135 Site5e_S95 Site5ee_S136 Site5f_S96 Site5ff_S137 Site5g_S97 Site5gg_S138 Site5h_S98 Site5k_S108 Site5m_S110 Site5n_S115 Site5o_S116 Site5p_S121 Site5q_S122 Site5r_S123 Site5s_S124 Site5u_S126 Site5v_S127 Site5w_S128 Site5z_S131; do
```

# Import reads onto QIIM 2

```{bash}
source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ../output/eDNA_mapping

qiime tools import \
  --type 'SampleData[PairedEndSequencesWithQuality]' \
  --input-path manifest.tsv \
  --input-format PairedEndFastqManifestPhred33V2 \
  --output-path demux.qza
```


# Check read quality

```{bash}
source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ../output/eDNA_mapping

qiime demux summarize \
  --i-data demux.qza \
  --o-visualization demux.qzv
```


# Remove primers

--p-front-f: the primer at the start of R1. ^ means “at the very start of the read”
--p-front-r: the primer at the start of R2
The part after ... is the other primer, flipped (reverse complement). The V9 region is short, so a read often runs past the end of it into the other primer. When that happens, cutadapt cuts off that primer and everything after it. ;optional means the read is kept even if this second primer isn’t there
--p-discard-untrimmed: throw away reads without the V9 primers
--p-nextseq-trim 20: trim low-quality bases from the read ends (a fix for the NextSeq sequencer)
--p-minimum-length 50: drop reads shorter than 50 bases after trimming


```{bash}
source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ../output/eDNA_mapping

qiime cutadapt trim-paired \
  --i-demultiplexed-sequences demux.qza \
  --p-front-f "^GTACACACCGCCCGTC...GTAGGTGAACCTGCAGAAGGATCA;optional" \
  --p-front-r "^TGATCCTTCTGCAGGTTCACCTAC...GACGGGCGGTGTGTAC;optional" \
  --p-discard-untrimmed \
  --p-nextseq-trim 20 \
  --p-minimum-length 50 \
  --p-cores 8 \
  --o-trimmed-sequences V9-demux.qza \
  --o-stats V9-cutadapt-stats.qza
```




# Clean up the reads with DADA2

```{bash}
source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ../output/eDNA_mapping

qiime dada2 denoise-paired \
  --i-demultiplexed-seqs V9-demux.qza \
  --p-trunc-len-f 0 \
  --p-trunc-len-r 0 \
  --p-n-threads 16 \
  --o-table V9-table.qza \
  --o-representative-sequences V9-rep-seqs.qza \
  --o-denoising-stats V9-dada2-stats.qza \
  --o-base-transition-stats V9-dada2-error-model.qza
```


Turn the DADA2 stats into a report you can view. It shows how many reads were kept at each step (input → filtered → denoised → merged → non-chimeric).

```{bash}
source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ../output/eDNA_mapping

qiime metadata tabulate \
  --m-input-file V9-dada2-stats.qza \
  --o-visualization V9-dada2-stats.qzv
```



# 6. Download a reference database (PR2)

To put a name on each ASV, we compare it with a reference database: DNA sequences from known organisms. For 18S we use PR2. The rescript plugin downloads it and converts it to QIIME 2 format.

```{bash}
source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
mkdir -p ../data/species_reference
cd ../data/species_reference

if [ ! -f pr2-seqs.qza ]; then
  qiime rescript get-pr2-data \
    --o-pr2-sequences pr2-seqs.qza \
    --o-pr2-taxonomy pr2-taxonomy.qza
fi
```




# 7. Name each ASV (assign taxonomy)

*vsearch* compares each ASV with the PR2 sequences. For each ASV it finds up to 10 reference sequences that are at least 90% identical, and gives the ASV the part of their names they mostly agree on.

--p-perc-identity 0.9: a reference must be at least 90% identical to count as a match
--p-maxrejects 100: stop searching after 100 non-matches (much faster, almost the same result)


```{bash}
source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ../output/eDNA_mapping

qiime feature-classifier classify-consensus-vsearch \
  --i-query V9-rep-seqs.qza \
  --i-reference-reads ../../data/species_reference/pr2-seqs.qza \
  --i-reference-taxonomy ../../data/species_reference/pr2-taxonomy.qza \
  --p-perc-identity 0.9 \
  --p-maxrejects 100 \
  --p-threads 16 \
  --o-classification V9-taxonomy.qza \
  --o-search-results V9-vsearch-hits.qza
```

change the taxonomic level (e.g. level 4 = class, level 5 = order)
sort samples by site to compare Site 1 and Site 5

```{bash}
source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ../output/eDNA_mapping

qiime taxa barplot \
  --i-table V9-table.qza \
  --i-taxonomy V9-taxonomy.qza \
  --m-metadata-file sample-metadata.tsv \
  --o-visualization V9-taxa-barplot.qzv
```


# Make my own barplot

1. qiime taxa collapse adds up the reads of all ASVs with the same name at one taxonomic level. Level 5 in PR2 is roughly “class” (e.g. Arthropoda, Dinophyceae)
2. qiime tools export takes the table out of the .qza file. It comes out as a .biom file
3. biom convert turns the .biom file into a tab-separated text file (.tsv)



```{bash}
source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ../output/eDNA_mapping

qiime taxa collapse \
  --i-table V9-table.qza \
  --i-taxonomy V9-taxonomy.qza \
  --p-level 5 \
  --o-collapsed-table V9-table-level5.qza

qiime tools export \
  --input-path V9-table-level5.qza \
  --output-path V9-table-level5

biom convert \
  --to-tsv \
  -i V9-table-level5/feature-table.biom \
  -o V9-table-level5.tsv
```


```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```


```{r Read the table}
# 1. skip the first comment line
counts <- read_tsv("../output/eDNA_mapping/V9-table-level5.tsv", skip = 1) # 1. skip the first comment line
```


```{r make barplot}

names(counts)[1] <- "taxon"

# 2. Shorten each name to its last named level
#    "d__Eukaryota;sgr__Obazoa;dv__Opisthokonta;dvs__Metazoa;c__Arthropoda" -> "Arthropoda"
counts$taxon <- gsub(";__", "", counts$taxon)        # drop empty levels
counts$taxon <- sub(".*;", "", counts$taxon)         # keep the last level
counts$taxon <- sub("^[a-z]+__", "", counts$taxon)   # drop the "c__" prefix

# 3. Make it "long": one row per sample per taxon
long <- counts %>%
  pivot_longer(-taxon, names_to = "sample", values_to = "reads")

# 4. Turn read counts into percent of each sample's reads
long <- long %>%
  group_by(sample) %>%
  mutate(percent = 100 * reads / sum(reads)) %>%
  ungroup()

# 5. Keep the 10 most common groups; lump the rest into "Other"
top10 <- long %>%
  group_by(taxon) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(percent)) %>%
  slice_max(total, n = 10) %>%
  pull(taxon)

long$taxon <- ifelse(long$taxon %in% top10, long$taxon, "Other")

# 6. Add the site, taken from the sample name ("Site1a_S83" -> "Site1")
long$site <- substr(long$sample, 1, 5)

# 7. Plot
ggplot(long, aes(x = sample, y = percent, fill = taxon)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~ site, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Sample", y = "Percent of reads", fill = "Group") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

```
